$comment: The radish raccoon (spec 277). The mesh arrived from Studio job dc3a200a with an auto-rig onto the `biped` family that could not be used -- measured off the file, its right knee sat 0.33 outside a body 0.5 wide, which is the ordinary failure of a humanoid auto-rig on an animal with no visible legs. So the skeleton is authored (`src/units/radish-raccoon-rig.ts`), the skin is built rather than solved (`src/units/radish-raccoon-skin.ts`), and the two clips are authored too (`src/units/radish-raccoon-clips.ts`). The mesh here is the unrigged generation stood up and re-centred, with the texture carried across verbatim; `npx tsx scripts/make-radish-raccoon.ts` writes it and the family's skeleton, and `npx tsx scripts/make-radish-raccoon-clips.ts` writes the clips and the library. Provenance below is what was actually charged for the generation. The state machine is three clips: an idle, a locomotion blend and a pounce. There is deliberately no `dead` parameter and no terminal state, because `driveUnit` writes a parameter only if the document declares it and declaring one with no death clip behind it is a socket with nothing plugged into it. `swing` is `locking` rather than `oneshot`, which is what makes a committed blow uninterruptible -- the thing that category exists for -- and its 900ms is `melee.slash`'s whole wind-up plus follow-through, so the action timing below stretches the clip by exactly nothing. The blend tree reaches `run` at 40 rather than at the biped's 150 because there is no walk to sit between them -- 40 is the pace of the slowest thing on the map, so anything actually travelling is drawn running rather than at a fraction of a run.
